description: Human population of the San Juan-Carolina-Caguas metro area, 2010
source: US Census Bureau estimate in the CDC/PRDH data repository (Population_data/san_juan_population_data.csv)
notes: The case data cover this metro area. Island-wide Puerto Rico was 3.71 million in 2010 (PAHO).

description: Female Ae. aegypti per person (N_v = m * N_h)
source: Manore et al. 2014, Table 3: vector:host ratio 2:1, varied 1:1 to 10:1
notes: No San Juan field estimate. The 2010/11 fit fixes m * s0 at about 3.9, so the upper bound must reach 3.9 / s0. 20 covers s0 = 0.2; the s0 = 0.1 extreme needs 40.

description: Baseline biting rate (bites per mosquito per day)
source: Zahid et al. 2023 (Puerto Rico estimate from a systematic review); the gonotrophic cycle gives 0.25-0.33

description: Share of people using personal protection, beyond 2010 behaviour
source: Team plan prior range. Anchor: 44.8% of COPA participants (Ponce, 2018-19) used repellent in the past 30 days (Adams et al. 2022)
notes: No 2010 San Juan survey. Calibration keeps kappa = 0, so protection already in use in 2010 stays inside a0.

description: Share of bites prevented for a person who uses protection
source: DEET 23.8%: mean complete protection 301.5 minutes in the laboratory (Fradin & Day 2002). Skin repellents showed no significant effect on dengue in field studies (Bowman et al. 2016)
notes: No field estimate of per-bite efficacy; the range is an assumption. Calibration keeps eta = 0.

source: Manore et al. 2014, Table 3 (0.10-0.75); upper bound 1.0 from Andraud et al. 2012

description: Intrinsic incubation rate (1 / human incubation period)
source: Chan & Johansson 2012: mean 5.9 days, 95% between 3 and 10 days

description: Extrinsic incubation rate at San Juan's 1990-2013 mean temperature
source: Chan & Johansson 2012: mean extrinsic incubation 15 days at 25 C and 6.5 days at 30 C; NOAA station RQW00011641 (San Juan airport)
notes: Log-linear interpolation between the two published means. Weekly values for every season are in data/temperature_san_juan_weekly_1990_2013.csv (eps_v_per_day).

source: Gubler 1998: viremia lasts 4-5 days on average (range 2-12); Manore et al. 2014: infectious period 6 days (4-12)

description: Human birth and death rate (1 / life expectancy)
source: PAHO Core Indicators 2026: life expectancy at birth, Puerto Rico 2010 = 78.717 years (UN World Population Prospects 2024)
notes: The model assumes births = deaths. PAHO crude rates for 2010: 11.4 births and 10.2 deaths per 1,000.

description: Mosquito birth and death rate (1 / adult lifespan)
source: Manore et al. 2014, Table 3: lifespan 14 days (8-42); Brady et al. 2013 (survival under field conditions)

description: Share of DENV-1 infections that become a counted lab-positive case
source: Product of three factors: P(symptoms | infection) x P(reported | symptoms) x P(lab-positive | reported). See literature/evidence.md, section 2
notes: The case data fix only phi * s0, at about 0.0019. Baseline 0.005 is the value implied at s0 = 0.4.

description: Share of the population susceptible to DENV-1 on 30 Apr 2010
notes: No serotype-specific serosurvey for San Juan around 2010. Run 0.1 and 1.0 only as extremes.

description: Share of DENV-1 infections that cause symptoms (first factor of phi)
source: Wang et al. 2015 (DENV-1 towns: 11 inapparent per symptomatic infection); Bhatt et al. 2013 (about 1 in 4 worldwide); Argüello et al. 2015 (Puerto Rico, ages 10-18: 61.1% of infections inapparent)
notes: Studies define 'symptomatic' differently; the Puerto Rico cohort counted mild fevers from a diary.

description: Share of symptomatic cases reported to passive surveillance (second factor of phi)
source: Noyd & Sharp 2015: 10-27 cases went unreported for every case reported in the 1990s
notes: This is the team plan's p range. It is not phi.
